activities.caption: file the three kinds of knowledge
activities.name: epiKindsSort

config.prompt: Only one kind is the analysis's target — file all three:

items.label: a gymnast's routine she cannot state as propositions
knowing that the train leaves at nine
knowing that the earth orbits the sun

config.why: Only propositional knowledge can be true or false, only it can be justified by argument, and only it is the battleground below — though the three interpenetrate.

activities.anchor: That impossibility result reframed the whole post-1963 debate
activities.caption: true or false — the rules of definition
activities.name: epiDefJudge

statements.s: A real definition states conditions that are necessary and sufficient for the thing.
statements.why: Conditions X such that something counts as knowledge if and only if it has X.

statements.s: A single counterexample refutes a definition, exactly as it refutes "all swans are white".
statements.why: One case with all the stated conditions and without the thing — or vice versa — kills the analysis.

statements.s: Adding more internally accessible conditions eventually makes a definition Gettier-proof.
statements.why: Zagzebski's result: any definition built from internal conditions plus truth can be Gettiered — a lucky accident rescues the truth whatever you add.

statements.s: Defining knowledge is the same game as defining water — find the underlying essence.
statements.why: Except the samples are episodes of knowing, and every episode can be rigged.

activities.anchor: a believer who wins the lottery by a hunch does not know the winning number
activities.caption: fill the blanks — what each clause excludes
activities.name: epiTriCloze

config.text: Each clause of the tripartite analysis earns its place by excluding a specific failure: no %%0%% (indifference), no %%1%% (error), no %%2%% (luck).
config.hint: The three conditions, each guarding against one failure.

activities.anchor: the evidence that justified it points at Jones
activities.caption: rebuild the Gettier sandwich
activities.name: epiGettierOrder

config.prompt: Rebuild the Gettier sandwich — two failures with justification laundered in between:
items: Bad luck: Jones doesn't get the job
Your evidence justifies the Jones-based belief
Good luck: you get the job and coincidentally have ten coins
The implied belief comes out true — by luck alone
config.why: The luck gap between justification and truth is the thing every repair below is trying to close.

activities.anchor: Four families of response, each a serious position with costs
activities.caption: pair each repair with its cost
activities.name: epiRepairsMatch

config.prompt: Four families of repair — pair each with its cost:

pairs.right: kills the original cases but not refined ones — too narrow
closes every luck gap by force, at the price of admitting almost nothing is known
knowledge without internally accessible justification — the externalism is the controversy
humanises reliabilism but inherits the same externalist debates

config.why: Gettier cases fail because luck, not virtue or a reliable process, produced the truth — the analysis moved outward, not away.

activities.anchor: answered centuries later with common-sense defiance
activities.caption: drag the divider — two answers to the sceptic
activities.name: epiMooreCompare

config.prompt: Drag the divider — two answers to the sceptic:

before.label: Descartes rebuilds
before.text: Doubt everything doubtable — perception, memory, the dream and demon arguments — and rebuild from the one unshakable base: I think, therefore I am.

after.label: Moore waves his hand
after.text: "Here is one hand; therefore an external world exists" — more certain, Moore argued, than any premise used against it.

config.why: The modern serious version is narrower: what justifies trusting perception, memory and induction at all — and the standards for surveys, instruments and AI systems are applied reliabilism.

activities.anchor: Beneath the sources sits the oldest problem of all
activities.caption: file the Agrippa trilemma's three endings
activities.name: epiAgrippaSort

config.prompt: Every chain of justification ends one of three ways — file the endings:

items.label: the chain of reasons runs back forever
justification as mutual support — a web rather than a tower
bedrock claims accepted without further proof
Descartes' search for the unshakable base

config.why: Every epistemologist since antiquity has paid one of those three prices — and the choice shapes how much science can establish, what a court may presume, when an argument may rest.
